title: Inside a Transformer Block
tagline: Step the residual stream through one block and watch attention mix positions while the FFN works on each alone
summary: A transformer is a stack of identical blocks, and every block edits a running residual stream with six little moves. Press Step to walk one block end to end: LayerNorm, self-attention (whose n x n weight matrix blends value vectors across positions), a residual add, LayerNorm again, a position-wise feed-forward network, and a final residual add. A live block diagram highlights the active sublayer while heatmaps show the actual numbers, making the core lesson obvious: attention is the only place information moves between tokens, the FFN processes each token on its own, and the residual stream only ever changes at the two adds.
highlights: Step one transformer block through all six moves and watch a live block diagram light up the active sublayer.
See the n x n attention matrix and how each output row becomes a weighted blend of value vectors across positions.
Confirm the residual stream changes only at the two '+' adds — LayerNorm, attention and the FFN all compute on a branch first.
Contrast attention (mixes information between positions) with the feed-forward network (transforms each position independently).
Read off why residual connections plus pre-norm LayerNorm are what let dozens of these blocks stack and still train.
